To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we demonstrate that electrodeposited Schottky diode on highly doped n-Ge show low off current and low series resistance.
electrodeposited Schottky diode contacts on highly doped germanium are suitable for limiting leakage current in Ge-based pMOSFETs.

we have demonstrated that electrodeposited nickel and nickel germanide Schottky contacts to highly doped germanium are promising candidates for the source/drain contacts of Ge channel p-MOSFETS, as they exhibit low leakage currents and low series resistances.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of high-quality Schottkky contacts for Ge-based Schottky barrier MOSFETs to limit the leakage current.
the development of a high-performance Ge channel PMOSFET.
the fabrication and characterization of high-quality Schottkey diodes on highly n-doped Ge.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
NiGe Schottky contacts are suitable for high-performance p-MOSFETS.
the use of Ni-Ge and/or NiGe Schottky contacts on n-Ge is highly promising for Ge channel SB PMOSFETs, as they exhibit low series resistance and low leakage current.
NiGe/Ge SB diodes are a promising candidate for SB Ge channel PMOSFETs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Ni-Ge and/or NiGe/Ge contacts are promising for the realization of low-leakage Ge p-MOSFETS.
the use of Ni-Ge Schottkey diodes in Ge channel PMOSFETs would allow the use of highly doped substrates for suppressing subthreshold leakage currents.
the Ni-Ge and the NiGe/Ge SB contacts are promising candidates for the realization of Ge-based SB p-MOS devices with a low leakage current.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of NiGe Schottky contacts in the source/dain region of SB p-MOS devices could enable the fabrication of high-performance devices with low off current.
electrodeposited Schottky contacts on Ge are suitable for low off-current Ge-based SB PMOSFETs.
the use of Ni-Ge and/or NiGe/Ge as Schottky contacts in SB Ge p-MOSFETS is promising.
